subtype: Approach: protecting privacy and safety while building [Action]
passage: “Devika, you asked how our class website avoided drama. I'm Asif, and I'll be honest, I almost skipped the boring part. We wanted photos of everyone. First I asked each classmate in person, and two said no. So those two appear as drawings we made together. The site shows first names only, no phone numbers, no school address, no class timetable. Before we published anything I showed the whole plan to our class teacher, who asked, ‘Who can see this?’ We changed it so only people with the link can open it, and the link goes through the class group, not the open internet. It took an extra week. But nobody woke up to find a stranger looking at their photo.”

qa.q: What names does the site show?
What might Asif have been worried about while planning?
qa.a: That strangers might see classmates' photos and cause them harm or discomfort, which is why Asif asked everyone and showed the teacher.

qa.q: What else could Asif do to keep the site safe, and why?
qa.a: Check the site regularly and remove anything a classmate later wants taken down, since a person's consent can change.

qa.q: How does the plan look to a classmate who said no to a photo?
qa.a: That classmate feels respected because the refusal was accepted and a drawing was used instead.

grounding: A teen making a class website asks permission for photos, uses first names only and shows the plan to a teacher.

subtype: Approach: protecting privacy and safety while building [Action]
passage:
I'm Manjula, and I sit two rows behind Mahima, so I watched her class-website plan unfold. On Monday she went desk to desk with a printed list of our names and a question: “Can I put your photo on the class page? Yes, no, or only in a group?” She ticked each answer. Three people said no. She crossed their names off the photo list without arguing.
On Tuesday I noticed she'd changed the captions: first names only, no surnames, no school name at the top, no mention of which bus stop we use.
On Wednesday she took her laptop to Mrs Pillai, our class teacher, and I saw them scroll through it together. Mrs Pillai pointed at something, and Mahima blurred one photo where a house number showed behind two kids.
The site went up on Friday. I checked. My photo was in the group one, like I'd asked.

qa.q: What three answers could classmates give about their photos?
qa.a: Yes, no, or only in a group.

qa.q: What does Mahima crossing off names without arguing suggest?
qa.a: It suggests she felt the refusals were fair and was comfortable, even respectful, about them, putting classmates' choice above having more photos.

qa.q: What else could Mahima do to keep the site safe over time?
qa.a: Share the link only within the class and ask again before adding any new photos.

qa.q: How does the finished site feel to Manjula?
qa.a: Manjula feels respected, since the photo appeared exactly as asked, only in the group one.

grounding: A classmate sees a teen ask each person's permission, use first names only and check the class site with a teacher before it goes online.

subtype: Approach: protecting privacy and safety while building [Action]
passage:
Monday: Lalremsiami has a draft of the girls' football team site ready: full names, shirt numbers, photos, and the time of every Saturday practice at the ground. Gurpreet, the goalkeeper, looks at it and says quietly, “My uncle doesn't let me post photos.” Lalremsiami stops, then deletes the practice timings too.
Wednesday: She sends each of the fourteen players a message: “Photo OK? Name OK? Reply yes or no.” Two say no to photos; she replaces theirs with the team crest. All names become first names only.
Friday: She shows the page to the sports teacher, who asks her to make it visible by link only and remove the ground's name. She does both before sharing the link in the team group. Gurpreet's slot shows the crest and “Gurpreet, keeper”.

qa.q: How many players did Lalremsiami message?
What might Lalremsiami have been feeling when she stopped on Monday?
qa.a: She was probably startled and uneasy, realising her draft exposed teammates in ways she had not thought about 😰

qa.q: What else could protect the team on this site?
qa.a: Posting match results rather than future practice times, so strangers cannot tell where the girls will be and when.

qa.q: How is the finished page for Gurpreet?
qa.a: Gurpreet is included and safe: the crest stands in for the photo, with just a first name and position.

grounding: Shows a teen building a team site who asks each player's permission, uses first names only and runs the page past a teacher before sharing.
